paper_id: AceCoder_ Utilizing Existing Code to Enhance Code Generation
title: AceCoder: Utilizing Existing Code to Enhance Code Generation
motivation: LLM prompting techniques for NLP underperform on code generation; existing methods lack task-specific design for software requirements and implementation.
problem_framing: Code generation faces two distinct challenges: requirement understanding (what to write) and code implementation (how to write). Current prompts fail to address either.
key_insight: Human developers use test cases to clarify requirements and search for similar code for reuse; LLMs can be guided to do the same through structured prompts with preliminaries and retrieved examples.
method_signature: Retrieve similar programs, select diverse examples, construct prompts with <requirement, preliminary, code> triples, guide LLM to output intermediate then final code.
evaluation_criteria: Pass@1/3/5 accuracy on MBPP/MBJP/MBJS benchmarks; human preference rating on correctness, code smell, maintainability.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: REDCODER (fine-tuned retrieval model) performs poorly due to overfitting on limited training data; when retrieval is irrelevant, AceCoder degrades to few-shot prompting.
evidence_for_taste: existing prompting techniques are designed for natural language generation
human developers often use some software artifacts
directly selecting top-k retrieved programs is unreasonable
AceCoder degrades to few-shot prompting at worst
thinking_moves: Identifies two root causes of LLM code generation failure: requirement ambiguity and implementation knowledge gaps
Maps observed human behaviors (TDD, code reuse) into explicit LLM prompting mechanisms
Treats prompt design as a search problem with constraints (token limit, redundancy elimination)
Ablates each module to verify necessity rather than assuming modularity
Validates via human preference beyond automatic metrics, recognizing code quality is not fully captured by pass rates
